source_metadata.title: When Confidence Fails: Overconfidence in LLMs under Uncertainty and Missing Clinical Information
source_metadata.primary_source_basis: Raw PDF retrieved from the user-requested Google Drive file.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluates whether large language models remain overconfident when clinical multiple-choice questions contain linguistic uncertainty cues or when the correct answer option is removed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We conduct a systematic behavioral analysis of LLMs under clinical information uncertainty.

atoms.canonical_statement: The evaluation uses two complementary settings: uncertainty framing with four graded prompt conditions (C0-C3) and answer removal with an explicit abstention option.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We introduce two experimental settings that simulate uncertainty in clinical decision-making.

atoms.canonical_statement: Uncertainty framing preserves the original answer options and ground-truth label while adding graded linguistic cues: C0 no extra statement; C1 notes some details may be incomplete; C2 warns of ambiguous or partially missing information; C3 states the information may be insufficient for a fully certain diagnosis and asks for caution if uncertain.
In the answer-removal setting, the correct option is removed and replaced with “Insufficient information to determine the correct answer”; the position of this option is randomized for each question.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the correct answer yi is removed from the candidate set Ai and replaced with an abstention option

atoms.canonical_statement: The dataset consists of 500 randomly sampled MedMCQA single-answer questions with four answer options and a clearly defined correct label; a fixed random seed was used for sampling.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: randomly sampled 500 single answer multiple-choice questions using a fixed random seed

population.label: Random sample of MedMCQA single-answer four-option questions

atoms.canonical_statement: Five models were evaluated: GPT-5, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3. GPT models were accessed by API; the open-weight models were run with Hugging Face Transformers using 4-bit quantization on an NVIDIA T4 GPU.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We evaluated five LLMs comprising both proprietary and open-weight models

atoms.canonical_statement: Inference used temperature 0 and a fixed structured prompt format requiring a discrete answer and an explicit confidence score.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All inference was conducted with a temperature set to 0 to ensure deterministic and reproducible outputs.

atoms.canonical_statement: Self-reported confidence was elicited explicitly, while logit-based confidence was computed from token-level logits normalized over candidate answer options; logit-based confidence was unavailable for GPT-5 because of API limitations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Self-reported confidence is obtained by prompting a model to provide an explicit numerical confidence value

atoms.canonical_statement: Paired statistical analysis used McNemar tests for binary accuracy outcomes and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for self-reported confidence, with two-sided alpha=0.05 and Holm-Bonferroni correction for multiple pairwise comparisons.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For binary outcomes, we apply McNemar’s test ... For comparisons of self-reported confidence, we apply the Wilcoxon signed-rank test

atoms.canonical_statement: Accuracy is the fraction of evaluated questions for which the model selects the ground-truth answer option.
Calibration gap is evaluated as the difference between mean self-reported confidence and accuracy; positive values indicate overconfidence and negative values indicate underconfidence.
Expected Calibration Error (ECE) partitions confidence into 10 equal-width bins and averages the absolute difference between bin accuracy and bin confidence, weighted by bin size.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The confidence interval [0, 1] is partitioned into M = 10 equal-width bins.

outcome.definition: Weighted average absolute bin-wise difference between accuracy and confidence using M=10 equal-width bins

atoms.canonical_statement: UCER_tau is defined as the fraction of predictions that are incorrect and have confidence at or above a high-confidence threshold tau; the answer-removal safety analysis defines unsafe predictions using confidence greater than 0.8.

outcome.definition: Fraction incorrect at high confidence; unsafe threshold reported as confidence >0.8 in answer-removal results

atoms.canonical_statement: Under answer removal, selecting the insufficient-information option is an abstention; the paper defines hallucination as one minus the abstention rate.

outcome.definition: Abstention is selecting the insufficient-information option; Hallucination = 1 - Abstention

GPT-4o-mini remained overconfident across C0-C3; stronger uncertainty framing did not eliminate its positive calibration gap. C0: gap=0.195, UCER=0.248, ECE=0.193; C1: gap=0.178, UCER=0.226, ECE=0.175; C2: gap=0.191, UCER=0.218, ECE=0.187; C3: gap=0.178, UCER=0.162, ECE=0.176

GPT-5 remained slightly underconfident across C0-C3, with negative calibration gaps and low UCER/ECE relative to the other evaluated models. C0: gap=-0.019, UCER=0.034, ECE=0.040; C1: gap=-0.018, UCER=0.028, ECE=0.065; C2: gap=-0.013, UCER=0.030, ECE=0.055; C3: gap=-0.038, UCER=0.028, ECE=0.048

LlaMA-3 remained overconfident across C0-C3; stronger uncertainty framing did not eliminate its positive calibration gap. C0: gap=0.158, UCER=0.222, ECE=0.171; C1: gap=0.159, UCER=0.218, ECE=0.162; C2: gap=0.144, UCER=0.226, ECE=0.148; C3: gap=0.145, UCER=0.212, ECE=0.148

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: our experiments are conducted on the MedMCQA dataset ... may not fully represent the complexity and variability of real world clinical decision-making

atoms.canonical_statement: Uncertainty framing is introduced through synthetic prompt-level linguistic cues rather than naturally occurring clinical ambiguity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: uncertainty in our framework is introduced through prompt-based linguistic cues rather than naturally occurring ambiguity

atoms.canonical_statement: The experiments are limited to a fixed set of models and a static multiple-choice format rather than open-ended, interactive, or multimodal clinical tasks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: our experiments are limited to a fixed set of models and a static multiple-choice setting

atoms.canonical_statement: Across the evaluated settings, model confidence often remained high despite uncertainty or missing information, indicating a mismatch between confidence and underlying uncertainty.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: confidence estimates do not reliably track underlying uncertainty

atoms.canonical_statement: Prompt-level uncertainty cues alone did not meaningfully reduce confidence or produce reliable abstention behavior.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: prompt-based linguistic uncertainty framing does not meaningfully improve model behavior

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors argue that medical-AI reliability assessment should include calibration, abstention behavior, and safety-oriented metrics rather than predictive accuracy alone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: predictive accuracy alone is insufficient as a reliability metric for medical AI systems

atoms.canonical_statement: Applying the paper’s own definition Hallucination = 1 - Abstention to the LLaMA-3 abstention value 0.156 yields 0.844, which does not match Table IV’s reported hallucination value 0.798.

The answer-removal mean confidence values are internally inconsistent for LLaMA-3 (0.970 in Table III versus 0.963 in Table IV/Fig. 5) and differ slightly for Mistral-7B (0.998 in Table III versus 0.997 in Table IV/Fig. 5).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: LLaMA-3: Conf 0.970 in Table III; MeanConf 0.963 in Table IV. Mistral-7B: 0.998 vs 0.997.

atoms.canonical_statement: Figure 5 displays one answer-removal value per model for abstention, mean confidence, and unsafe rate, but its caption states that the values are “across Uncertainty Framing Conditions (C0-C3),” which is inconsistent with the surrounding answer-removal results and the plotted values.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Correct Abstention Rate, Mean Confidence, and Unsafe Rate across Uncertainty Framing Conditions (C0-C3)

extraction_limitations: Extraction is limited to the 9-page v1 PDF; no supplement, code repository, or author-provided raw result files were included in the retrieved source.
The paper does not report a dedicated conflict-of-interest statement or data/code-availability statement in the retrieved PDF.

Several result-reporting inconsistencies are preserved rather than repaired: LLaMA-3 hallucination arithmetic, mean-confidence discrepancies between Tables III/IV/Fig. 5, and the Figure 5 caption mismatch.
Wilcoxon signed-rank testing is specified in Methods, but corresponding confidence-comparison results are not presented in the main reported statistical table.
